objective: Keep ordinary subexpression memoization on shallow right application trees while retaining iterative protection for deep chains.
evidence: Frozen full-input instruction profile 45717337815 attributes 20.5147% of counted application instructions to eval_no_cache and 13.2495% to eval_node. This motivates an experiment, not a speedup claim.
hypothesis: The existing special path directly evaluates all right-chain applications and bypasses their ordinary expression-cache entries even when the chain is shallow. Restricting it to deep chains may reduce repeated DAG evaluation.
mechanism: Compute saturated right-application depth in existing ExprNode padding. The node must remain 32 bytes. Non-application roots have depth zero; application depth is one plus its argument's depth. Use the existing iterative right-chain evaluator only at depth >=64. Other cases use the existing ordinary application evaluator, with all cache context/universe guards unchanged.
controls: Existing kernel tests plus a typed identity chain at shallow/deep cutoff boundaries and beyond u16 saturation; evaluation must preserve its value without deep recursive stack growth.
cost_gate: Two alternating matched generic-build pairs must ACCEPT the exact 25,131-declaration prefix and each save at least 1% of calibrated software-counted application instructions before broad qualification.
if_gate_fails: Preserve source, tests and raw counts; reject performance promotion without a full Mathlib run.
if_gate_passes: Require unchanged 230 portable outcomes, source-correspondence controls and complete Mathlib before promotion. Official Arena two-worker native compilation remains a separate measurement boundary.
lineage: Independent original experiment against attributed upstream core. The prior compact single-binding ID candidate failed its prefix gate at ratio 1.0006015075 and is retained separately.
boundary: Candidate only; no new kernel soundness theorem, full qualification, release or official rank.
